answer: Proposal "cedar": one identity per attested chip. A secure enclave's manufacturer-signed attestation proves its key sits in unique silicon; the ledger registers each attested key once and weights voice by it. Ten aliases then need ten devices — real ferrous hardware, not costumes — so silicon scarcity replaces clone detection and cheap farms find no haven. Trusted assumption: the fab embeds one key per chip; a compromised fab mints sybils freely. Cost stays linear in devices, so the defense holds only while amortized device cost per epoch exceeds per-identity reward.
